speaker: AIDEN
text: The room had rose petals on the bed, Shawna said, but Dante was gathering them in his hands and putting them in the ice bucket.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She was still wearing her wedding dress.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: Are they bothering you?

speaker: AIDEN
text: she'd asked.

speaker: DANTE
text: They got dirt on them.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: Dante.

speaker: DANTE
text: I don't want you sleeping in dirt.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She had laughed and kicked off her shoes. He had watched them hit the carpet as if he hadn't quite believed she intended to stay.

speaker: AIDEN
text: That part fucked with me. I knew exactly how that man had looked at her shoes. I'd looked at her watch the same way, checking whether she'd put anything down long enough to live with me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna kept talking.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante sat beside the bucket full of roses and told her he'd been in prison before they met. Nine months of his life, a little more than three years before this morning in my bedroom. He'd been twenty-eight then. His first afternoon, a man at the next table spilled soup down the front of an older prisoner's shirt. The older man looked down at himself,

speaker: AIDEN
text: then carried on eating.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante waited.

speaker: B01C07_PRISON_BULLY_1
text: You hear me, old man?

speaker: AIDEN
text: the first man said.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: I heard you.

speaker: B01C07_PRISON_BULLY_1
text: Then look at me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The older prisoner put his spoon down.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: You have my soup on your hand.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The man slapped him.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante got up.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He told Shawna he didn't remember crossing the space between the tables. One minute he was sitting down. The next he was holding the man against a wall with blood on his own shirt, shouting for someone to bring the old man another fucking bowl.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "What happened after the soup?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: I asked Shawna.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: "I just told you."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "You told me a nigga got hit. Baby, you skipped the part where the nigga found out."

speaker: AIDEN
text: She looked at me for a second. Then she settled farther back against the pillows.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: "Dante said the man had three friends."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "There we go."

speaker: AIDEN
text: The first friend got up when Dante crossed the room. A big man with a shaved head and a towel over one shoulder, forty years old and proud of how much space he took from everybody around him. He put himself between Dante and the older man.

speaker: B01C07_PRISON_BULLY_2
text: "Sit your ass down."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante kept walking.

speaker: B01C07_PRISON_BULLY_2
text: "Nigga, you deaf?"

speaker: DANTE
text: "No. You finished?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: The man swung. Dante caught the edge of it across his jaw and hit him with the tray he'd still been carrying. Food went everywhere. A cup rolled off the table and broke under somebody's shoe.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Then everybody stood up.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The man who'd spilled the soup grabbed Marcellus by his collar. He was smiling at Dante, enjoying how quickly a stranger had given him something useful to hurt.

speaker: B01C07_PRISON_BULLY_1
text: "You want the old nigga? Come get him."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante went over the table.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna lifted one hand when she told me. I could see her husband for a second in the shape she made: feet off the floor, hands already reaching, a man who'd decided the space between him and somebody in trouble belonged to him now.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I knew that decision. I didn't like sharing it with him, but nigga, I knew it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante hit the man holding Marcellus with both knees. They went down together. The old man fell against the bench, caught himself, and picked up his soup spoon before anybody stepped on it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "He picked up the spoon?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: I asked.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: "He liked that spoon."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga, I respect an attachment."

speaker: AIDEN
text: The third man came behind Dante with a chair. Marcellus saw him first. He put a foot against the man's ankle as he passed, just enough to spoil the step, and the chair struck the table instead of Dante's head.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante turned into him.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He told Shawna he never knew which part of the fight broke his finger. He remembered the pain later. What he remembered then was getting that chair away, seeing the old man standing up again, hearing men all around them shout because somebody had finally interrupted the same ugly afternoon they'd been living for years.

speaker: AIDEN
text: By the time the guards came, the soup was on the floor and three men were finding new reasons to stay there.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante stood in the middle of it with blood on his shirt.

speaker: DANTE
text: "Another bowl,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: he said.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The nearest guard pointed at the door.

speaker: B01C07_GUARD
text: "Move."

speaker: DANTE
text: "Nigga, the old man ain't eaten."

speaker: B01C07_GUARD
text: "Move now."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus put a hand on his shoulder.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: "I can wait."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante looked at the empty bowl on the table. Then at the men on the floor. Then he picked up the bowl and put it in the guard's hand.

speaker: DANTE
text: "So can they."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna smiled when she remembered that part. I let her have the smile. Her dead man had earned that much.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Three niggas,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: I said.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: "Three."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "I had twelve."

speaker: AIDEN
text: She hit me with a pillow so gently even my bullet didn't complain.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: "You asked for the story."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "I'm listening. Nigga can listen and hold the record."

speaker: AIDEN
text: She laughed, and for a second Dante wasn't sitting between us anymore. He was somewhere behind her, where she could turn and see him without leaving my bed.

speaker: AIDEN
text: It bought him punishment and a friendship.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The old man's name was Marcellus Vale.

speaker: AIDEN
text: When Dante came back, Marcellus was sitting on his bunk with a little paper box in his hands. Inside was a broken plastic comb, several buttons, and a gold-colored wrapper folded into a heart.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: For your trouble,

speaker: AIDEN
text: he said.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante looked at the heart.

speaker: DANTE
text: Nigga, what am I supposed to do with this?

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: Give it to somebody.

speaker: DANTE
text: A woman?

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: If you like women.

speaker: DANTE
text: I like women.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: Then perhaps one will like a heart.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante took it. The folds were so small and straight they looked pressed by a machine.

speaker: DANTE
text: You make jewelry?

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: I did.

speaker: DANTE
text: Used to steal it myself.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus looked up.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: Then we may have met professionally.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante laughed. The old man didn't, but he moved over so Dante could sit.

speaker: AIDEN
text: For two months they ate together. Marcellus taught him cards. Dante taught him which men to leave alone and which men only wanted somebody to be frightened of them. Marcellus had already been inside for years. He knew the difference. He let Dante tell him anyway.

speaker: AIDEN
text: At night, the old man held a photograph under the light from the corridor.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Celeste stood on a little stage with a microphone in her hand. Her mouth was open. Her eyes were closed. A blue stone lay at the base of her throat.

speaker: DANTE
text: Your wife?

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante asked one night.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: Yes.

speaker: DANTE
text: She beautiful.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: I know.

speaker: DANTE
text: She still come see you?

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus turned the photograph over.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: No.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante didn't ask again until the day a letter arrived and Marcellus sat with it unopened through dinner.

speaker: DANTE
text: You want me to read it?

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante said.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: I know what it says.

speaker: DANTE
text: Then why they send it?

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: Because some people think they can finish a love affair by closing a bank account.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Dante sat on the other bunk.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus stared at the envelope.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: She died three months ago.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Neither man said anything for a while.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Then Dante asked about the diamond.

speaker: AIDEN
text: When Marcellus first saw the stone, it didn't look like forty million dollars. It looked like a dirty piece of sky somebody had knocked loose and tried to bury.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He bought it from a man who carried it in an empty cigarette packet. He paid too much, threatened two people who thought they were entitled to part of it, and came home with an empty account and a fist-sized bruise on his jaw.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Celeste was frying chicken.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She took one look at him and turned the burner down.

speaker: CELESTE
text: How much?

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: Wait until you see it.

speaker: CELESTE
text: How much, Marcellus?

speaker: AIDEN
text: He put the cigarette packet on the table.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She looked inside. Then she looked at him.

speaker: CELESTE
text: We are not eating that.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He took the stone from her and held it toward the kitchen window. Light passed through the rough blue surface and laid a strange little shape across her white sleeve.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She stopped looking angry for a moment.

speaker: CELESTE
text: Oh,

speaker: AIDEN
text: she said.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He watched her instead of the stone.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: Yes.

speaker: AIDEN
text: It took him months to cut it. He worked in a room behind their house, shut the door, and disappeared for days at a time while Celeste sang at a lounge that barely paid her. She brought him food. Half the time it was still there when she came back.

speaker: AIDEN
text: At the end of the first month, she moved his pillow into the workshop.

speaker: AIDEN
text: At the end of the second, she put a photograph of herself beside the lamp.

speaker: CELESTE
text: So you remember who the fuck lives out here,

speaker: AIDEN
text: she told him.

speaker: AIDEN
text: At the end of the third, he came into the lounge wearing his good suit.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Celeste was halfway through a song. The piano player saw Marcellus coming and lost his place. Celeste stopped, turned, and saw the little box in her husband's hands.

speaker: CELESTE
text: Don't you propose to me again,

speaker: AIDEN
text: she said into the microphone.

speaker: CELESTE
text: I fell for that shit once.

speaker: AIDEN
text: People laughed. Marcellus kept walking until he reached the stage.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: I made you something.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She came down the steps. He opened the box.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The room got quiet.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The stone was blue in a way Dante later told Shawna he couldn't explain. Shawna told me he held her hand against the lamp trying to show her what Marcellus meant. Blue that deepened when you moved it away from the light. Blue that kept looking wet after you understood it was dry.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Celeste put her fingers over her mouth.

speaker: CELESTE
text: Marcellus.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He lifted the necklace out.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: Turn around.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She did. He fastened it behind her neck. The diamond rested against her skin, surrounded by little pale stones that made it look even darker.

speaker: CELESTE
text: What'd you call it?

speaker: AIDEN
text: she asked.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: Blue Mercy.

speaker: CELESTE
text: Mercy for what?

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: The last three months.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She put her arms around him and kissed him in front of everybody.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Somewhere in that room, a man saw forty million dollars. Valentino was sitting near the back with Red, who was twenty-eight at the time and hungry for more than he could afford.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Celeste saw her husband coming home from the little room behind the house.

speaker: AIDEN
text: That's the shit Marcellus told Dante. Dante told his new wife. And his wife sat beside me years later with another dead man's necklace in my fist, telling me about all of them.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I wanted to interrupt her. I wanted to ask whether Dante kissed better than me, whether he had ever promised her more, whether this old nigga's beautiful wife had looked at him the way mine looked at a fucking watch.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I kept my mouth shut.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, I wanted to hear what happened more than I wanted to hear myself.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red came to the workshop two weeks later with T and a bottle of wine that cost more than Marcellus's first car.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He said he wanted to buy the stone.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus said it wasn't for sale.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red doubled the number he'd been planning to offer before he even said it.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: It belongs to my wife,

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus told him.

speaker: RED
text: Then ask your wife.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: She isn't for sale either.

speaker: AIDEN
text: T laughed. Red didn't.

speaker: AIDEN
text: They left the wine on the table.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Celeste came in afterward, read the label, and carried it straight to the sink.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus caught her wrist.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: Do you know what that's worth?

speaker: CELESTE
text: Yes.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She pulled free and poured it out.

speaker: CELESTE
text: That's why I don't want to find out what we owe him if we drink it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: But money was tight. A stone worth a fortune didn't pay the electric bill if nobody intended to sell it. Marcellus agreed to exhibit it at a private showing Valentino arranged. A rich client wanted jewelry made in the same blue setting. Other men wanted to pay him just to look at stones they already owned.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He told Celeste it would give him enough work to stop worrying.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She asked whether he would ever have enough work to stop.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Before the showing, he made a duplicate. A lesser blue stone, convincing under warm light, in an identical necklace. He could leave that in the display while Celeste wore the original. He marked the removable mounting in a place only he thought to check. The true diamond had its own tiny irregularity inside, older than anybody who'd ever owned it. No second stone could share

speaker: AIDEN
text: it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The men who came to the showing took both.

speaker: AIDEN
text: They took the necklaces, the loose jewels in the back room, and the book with his customers' names. T held Marcellus against his own workbench. Valentino lifted the necklace from Celeste's throat so carefully he didn't disturb her hair.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red stood in the doorway.

speaker: RED
text: Now,

speaker: AIDEN
text: he said,

speaker: RED
text: perhaps we can agree on a price.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus lunged at him. T hit him hard enough to knock the lamp over.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Celeste dropped to the floor beside her husband.

speaker: CELESTE
text: Take it,

speaker: AIDEN
text: she said to Red.

speaker: CELESTE
text: Go.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red looked down at her.

speaker: RED
text: You should've said that in the beginning.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He left an envelope on the workbench. There was a fraction of the money inside. Enough that he could say he'd paid. Not enough that any of them could mistake what had happened for a sale.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus stayed on the floor after they left.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Celeste held a towel against his face.

speaker: CELESTE
text: Look at me,

speaker: AIDEN
text: she kept saying.

speaker: CELESTE
text: It's gone. Look at me.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He was looking at her throat.

speaker: AIDEN
text: That was the part that made the old man's voice change when he told Dante.

speaker: AIDEN
text: His wife was right there. She was alive. She was asking him to look at her.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He could only see where the diamond had been.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He went after it. Of course he fucking went after it. By the time Shawna said that, I was standing beside the window imagining my own hands around Red's throat.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus went after the diamond in the same good suit he'd worn to give it away.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "He told Dante that?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: I asked.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: "He said Celeste tried to stop him."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "With words?"

speaker: SHAWNA
text: "With his car keys."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Smart woman."

speaker: AIDEN
text: He went in a taxi. Sat in the back with the gun in his coat and an envelope of money on his knee. Celeste stood in the doorway holding the keys he no longer needed. She didn't shout after him. That was the part he wished he could stop remembering.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The club Valentino owned had gold doors and a stairway lit from underneath. A singer Marcellus knew was onstage when he went in. She stopped halfway through a line when she saw his face.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Valentino sat in a private booth with two men.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus put the envelope on the table.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: "Your money."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Valentino looked inside. Smiled. Set it down again.

speaker: VALENTINO
text: "You came to buy something?"

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: "I came for what's mine."

speaker: AIDEN
text: The man on Valentino's right stood up. Marcellus hit him with the gun before he finished, and the man went across the table into a bottle of champagne.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The other man reached under his jacket.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus fired.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The sound stopped the whole room. The man fell back against the booth and slid down holding his shoulder. He lived. Marcellus would hear that again and again later, as if it were the part of the night he'd hoped to get wrong.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Valentino had disappeared behind the booth.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The old man went after him through a door beside the bar. A corridor. Another door. A room full of jewelry laid out beneath bright lights, rings and watches and little boxes bearing names he recognized.

speaker: AIDEN
text: His own tools sat on a table.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He picked one up. Turned it over. His initials were still there, small and careful, engraved when he'd first had enough money to believe he would own things for a long time.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The diamond wasn't.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Behind him a door opened. Two men came in from the corridor. Another appeared at the far end of the room.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus turned with the gun in his hand.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: "Where is it?"

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nobody answered.

speaker: AIDEN
text: The first blow took him behind the ear. He went against the table. Rings scattered across the floor. He tried to keep the gun up and couldn't. Somebody caught his wrist, somebody else hit his stomach, and the whole room tipped until his cheek was against the cold tiles among things he'd once made beautiful.

speaker: AIDEN
text: When the police came, Valentino stood in the doorway explaining what a dangerous man grief could make.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus could hear him.

speaker: AIDEN
text: That was why he tried to stand again.

speaker: AIDEN
text: That was why the men holding him wouldn't let him.

speaker: AIDEN
text: They carried him through the club past the singer, past the gold doors, past the taxi still waiting at the curb. The driver held up his meter like the night might still become ordinary if somebody paid for it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Celeste came to the station wearing slippers.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus saw them first. Little blue slippers with one heel crushed under her foot. She had hurried so much she hadn't put them on properly.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: "I didn't find it,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: he told her.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She looked at the blood on his face.

speaker: CELESTE
text: "I found you."

speaker: AIDEN
text: He couldn't answer her. He told Dante he'd spent eight years trying to get back to that moment with something better in his mouth.

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Nigga,"

speaker: AIDEN
text: I said when Shawna stopped,

speaker: AIDEN
text: "Red got to die."

speaker: AIDEN
text: She squeezed my hand.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: "Keep listening."

speaker: AIDEN
text: "I'm listening. That's what the listening is doing."

speaker: AIDEN
text: Marcellus went to prison.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Red opened the Saint with money raised against a diamond he said he'd bought from a respected jeweler. Marcellus read about it in a magazine somebody left in the visiting room.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Celeste visited him as long as she could.

speaker: AIDEN
text: At first she wore bright dresses and told him stories from the lounge. When he interrupted to ask which men had been asking about the necklace, she told him to eat the candy she'd brought.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Later she came less often because she was sick. He thought she was punishing him. They argued through the glass about a doctor she hadn't mentioned and money he couldn't send.

speaker: AIDEN
text: During her last visit, she wore the earrings he had made before either of them knew a man called Red.

speaker: CELESTE
text: I want you to do something,

speaker: AIDEN
text: she said.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: What?

speaker: CELESTE
text: Remember the first thing you ever gave me.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: The earrings.

speaker: CELESTE
text: No.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: The little bracelet.

speaker: CELESTE
text: No, Marcellus.

speaker: AIDEN
text: He looked at her, frightened now because he couldn't get it right.

speaker: CELESTE
text: A ride,

speaker: AIDEN
text: she said.

speaker: CELESTE
text: I was standing in the rain. You drove me home. You didn't ask for my number until we got there.

speaker: MARCELLUS
text: I remember.

speaker: CELESTE
text: Then remember that man too.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She put her hand against the glass.

speaker: AIDEN
text: After she died, a letter arrived among her things. Marcellus carried it until the folds began to split. One night he finally unfolded it in front of Dante and read it aloud.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna said Dante had written the words down after he got out because he was scared of forgetting them. He read them to her on their wedding night. She remembered the ones that mattered. When I met Marcellus later that day, he showed me the paper itself, and I read the rest with my own fucking eyes.

speaker: AIDEN
text: My love,

speaker: AIDEN
text: You think I never understood that stone. I did. I understood every hour you spent getting it right. I know the little words you hid beneath the blue mounting. I know you were waiting for me to find them, and I know you were disappointed when I liked the front so much I forgot to look behind it.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I found them the night you fell asleep with your shoes on. I was angry with you for missing supper. I took the necklace off and nearly dropped it, and there you were underneath, saying what you used to say at my door.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I came for you.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I wore those words against me every night afterward. You never asked whether I'd found them. You just watched me wear it and smiled.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I am so tired now, Marcellus. I can't keep driving out there. Don't let anybody tell you I stopped because I stopped loving you. I am stopping because I am sick, and I want the strength I have left for things that don't require me to pass through a locked door.

speaker: AIDEN
text: If you get your beautiful stone back, put it down before you touch somebody you love. I know your hands. They are warmer without all that metal in them.

speaker: AIDEN
text: And if you are still angry when you come home, be angry. You always were. Just open the curtains. Pay the piano man what I owe him. There is chicken in the freezer because I never learned how to cook for one.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I would take the ride again.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Celeste.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Shawna stopped.

speaker: AIDEN
text: Nigga, I was still facing the window. I didn't turn around until I could trust my fucking face.

speaker: AIDEN
text: What did Dante do?

speaker: AIDEN
text: I asked.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: He told Marcellus he'd get it back.

speaker: AIDEN
text: For a man he met in prison?

speaker: SHAWNA
text: For him. For her. For whatever he thought that would make him.

speaker: AIDEN
text: And you?

speaker: AIDEN
text: Her voice was small when she answered.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: I thought I married the kind of man who'd do that.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I nodded. I didn't like the dead nigga any better. I just had a harder time hating him the easy way.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: Dante took the three million first,

speaker: AIDEN
text: she said.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: He wanted money to get Marcellus a lawyer and buy us a way out when Red found out what else he wanted. He thought T would choose him. T was his brother.

speaker: AIDEN
text: But he didn't.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: No.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She lifted the watch.

speaker: SHAWNA
text: The last night Dante came home, he asked me whether this still looked too big on me. I told him everything he owned was too big on me. He said he'd put something in it that fit.

speaker: AIDEN
text: I looked at her.

speaker: AIDEN
text: What something?

speaker: SHAWNA
text: I thought he meant himself.

speaker: AIDEN
text: She worked the clasp open with shaking hands.

speaker: AIDEN
text: For the first time since I met her, the dead nigga was about to give us something we could use.
